sandbox: macOS sandbox-exec: no network, home folder unreadable, one scratch folder writable

tools.name: create_client
tools.description:
Create a WSGI client for testing applications without running a server.
    
    Args:
        application: The WSGI application to make requests to
        use_cookies: Persist cookies from Set-Cookie response headers to the Cookie 
            header in subsequent requests
    
    Returns:
        A werkzeug.Client instance for making requests to the WSGI application
    
    Example:
        >>> client = create_client(my_wsgi_app)
        >>> response = client.get('/')

tools.name: create_response
tools.description: Create a new response object with specified parameters. response: The data for the body of the response, defaults to empty body. status: The status code for the response, defaults to 200.

tools.name: response_text
tools.description: Get the response body as decoded UTF-8 text. response: The response body as string, bytes, or iterable of strings/bytes, e.g. b'hello' -> 'hello'.

tools.name: create_headers
tools.description:
Create a new headers object with optional initial values. defaults: An array of header key-value pairs to initialize the Headers object with, e.g. [['Content-Type', 'application/json'], ['X-Custom', 'value']] -> 'Content-Type: application/json
X-Custom: value

'.

tools.name: parse_accept_header
tools.description: Parse an Accept header and create an Accept object. value: The Accept header value to parse, e.g. 'text/html,application/json;q=0.9' -> 'text/html,application/json;q=0.9'

tools.name: parse_authorization_header
tools.description:
Parse an Authorization header value and create an Authorization object.
    
    Args:
        value: The header value to parse, e.g. "Basic dXNlcjpwYXNz"
        
    Returns:
        A dictionary with the authorization type and data, or None if empty.
        Example: {"auth_type": "basic", "data": {"username": "user", "password": "pass"}}

tools.name: parse_www_authenticate
tools.description:
Parse a ``WWW-Authenticate`` header value and create an instance of
    this class.
    
    :param value: The WWW-Authenticate header value to parse.
    
    Example: parse_www_authenticate('Bearer realm="example"') -> {'auth_type': 'bearer', 'values': {'realm': 'example'}}

tools.name: format_www_authenticate
tools.description:
Convert a WWWAuthenticate instance to a WWW-Authenticate header value.
    
    Args:
        auth_type: The authentication type (e.g., 'basic', 'digest')
        values: A dictionary of authentication parameters
        token: A token for authentication
    
    Returns:
        A WWW-Authenticate header value string
    
    Example:
        format_www_authenticate('basic') -> 'Basic'

tools.name: parse_content_security_policy
tools.description:
Parse a Content-Security-Policy header value and create an instance of the ContentSecurityPolicy class.
    
    Args:
        value: The Content-Security-Policy header value to parse
        
    Returns:
        A dictionary mapping directive names to their values
        
    Example:
        parse_content_security_policy("default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://example.com")
        -> {"default-src": "'self'", "script-src": "'self' https://example.com"}

tools.name: parse_etag
tools.description: Parse a quoted ETag value and create an instance of the ETag class, or None if the value is empty or invalid. value: The ETag value to parse, e.g. '"foo"' -> {'value': 'foo', 'weak': False}.

tools.name: format_etag
tools.description: Convert an ETag instance to an ETag header value. value: The ETag value, e.g. 'abc123' -> '"abc123"'. weak: Whether the ETag is weak, e.g. True -> 'W/"abc123"'.

tools.name: get_header_value
tools.description: Get the value of a header by key, returning None if the key is not found. headers: An object that stores headers with dict-like interface, key: The header key to look up.

tools.name: get_header_list
tools.description: Get all values for a header key as a list. headers: an object that stores headers with dict-like interface, key: the header key to retrieve all values for. Example: get_header_list({"Content-Type": ["text/html"], "Accept": ["application/json"]}, "Accept") -> ["application/json"]

tools.name: clear_headers
tools.description: Clear all headers from the headers object. headers: An object that stores headers with a dict-like interface -> None.

tools.name: parse_content_range
tools.description:
Parse a Content-Range header value and create an instance of the ContentRange class.
    
    Args:
        value: The Content-Range header value to parse, e.g. "bytes 200-400/1000"
        
    Returns:
        A dictionary with the ContentRange components: units, start, stop, length
        
    Example:
        parse_content_range("bytes 200-400/1000") -> {"units": "bytes", "start": 200, "stop": 401, "length": 1000}

tools.name: format_content_range
tools.description:
Convert a ContentRange instance to a Content-Range header value.
    
    Args:
        units: The units for the range, e.g., 'bytes'
        start: The start of the range
        stop: The end of the range (exclusive)
        length: The total length of the resource
        
    Returns:
        A Content-Range header value string
        
    Example:
        format_content_range('bytes', 0, 1023, 2048) -> 'bytes 0-1022/2048'

tools.name: parse_options_header
unquote_header_value
tools.description: Remove double quotes and backslash escapes from a header value. value: The header value to unquote, e.g. '"hello \"world\""' -> 'hello "world"'.

tools.name: parse_dict_header
tools.description: Parse a list header into a dictionary of key-value pairs. value: The header value to parse, e.g. 'a=b, c="d, e", f' -> {"a": "b", "c": "d, e", "f": None}.

tools.name: bind_map
tools.description:
Create a MapAdapter to match and build URLs based on request information.
    
    Args:
        server_name: The host:port of the request. The port is optional if it's the standard port for url_scheme.
        script_name: The URL path prefix under which the application is served, used to build URLs. Defaults to '/'.
        subdomain: The subdomain part of server_name, used when subdomain_matching is enabled.
        url_scheme: The protocol of the request. Used to match HTTP vs WebSocket rules, and when building external URLs.
        default_method: The HTTP method of the request.
        path_info: The path part after script_name, used to match rules. Defaults to '/'.
        query_args: The part of the URL after '?'. Used to preserve the args when redirecting during matching.
    
    Returns:
        A MapAdapter instance for URL matching and building.
    
    Example:
        >>> adapter = bind_map('example.com:8080', '/app', url_scheme='https')
        >>> # Use adapter to match or build URLs
tools.direct_call: werkzeug.routing.Map().bind(server_name, script_name, subdomain, url_scheme, default_method, path_info, query_args)

tools.name: check_password_hash
tools.description:
Securely check that the given stored password hash, previously generated using
    :func:`generate_password_hash`, matches the given password.

    Methods may be deprecated and removed if they are no longer considered secure. To
    migrate old hashes, you may generate a new hash when checking an old hash, or you
    may contact users with a link to reset their password.

    :param pwhash: The hashed password.
    :param password: The plaintext password.

    .. versionchanged:: 3.0
        All plain hashes are no longer supported.
    
    Example: check_password_hash("pbkdf2:sha256$150000$salt$hash", "password") -> True

tools.name: iri_to_uri
tools.description: Convert an IRI to a URI. All non-ASCII and unsafe characters are quoted. If the URL has a domain, it is encoded to Punycode. iri: The IRI to convert, e.g. 'http://☃.net/påth?q=èry%DF' -> 'http://xn--n3h.net/p%C3%A5th?q=%C3%A8ry%DF'.

tools.name: generate_debug_representation
tools.description: Create a debug representation of an object for better visualization in error messages. obj: any object to represent, e.g. {'a': 1} -> "<dict object at 0x...>".

tools.name: parse_http_cookies
tools.description: Parse cookies from a Cookie header into a dictionary. cookie: The Cookie header string to parse, e.g. 'sessionid=abc123; csrftoken=xyz789' -> {'sessionid': 'abc123', 'csrftoken': 'xyz789'}.

tools.name: set_http_cookie
tools.description:
Sets a cookie in the response with specified parameters like expiration and security flags.
    
    Args:
        key: the key (name) of the cookie to be set
        value: the value of the cookie
        max_age: should be a number of seconds, or None if the cookie should last only as long as the client's browser session
        path: limits the cookie to a given path, per default it will span the whole domain
        secure: If True, the cookie will only be available via HTTPS
        httponly: Disallow JavaScript access to the cookie
    
    Example:
        set_http_cookie("session_id", "abc123", max_age=3600, secure=True, httponly=True)

tools.name: delete_http_cookie
tools.description:
Deletes a cookie from the response, useful for session management or user logout.
    
    Args:
        key: the key (name) of the cookie to be deleted.
        path: if the cookie that should be deleted was limited to a path, the path has to be defined here.
        domain: if the cookie that should be deleted was limited to a domain, that domain has to be defined here.
    
    Example:
        delete_http_cookie("session_id", "/app", "example.com")
